```python
def count_rotation(arr):
    for i in range(len(arr) - 1):
        if arr[i] > arr[i + 1]:
            return i + 1
    return 0


assert count_rotation([3, 2, 1]) == 1
assert count_rotation([1, 2, 3]) == 0
assert count_rotation([3, 1, 2]) == 1
assert count_rotation([2, 3, 1]) == 2
assert count_rotation([4, 5, 1, 2, 3]) == 2
assert count_rotation([]) == 0
```

This is O(n) time and O(1) extra space. I checked each assert by hand against the code, but I didn't run it.

The GeeksforGeeks problem usually expects the index of the minimum element. That is the answer this code gives for rotated ascending arrays. For `[3,2,1]` the minimum is at index 2, so the standard answer would be 2. Your assert expects 1, so the code follows your assert rather than the standard definition.
